---
title: "The bundled datasets"
subtitle: "Provenance and dictionaries for the SAR and Cao–Dowd case studies"
---

Three panels ship inside the wheel as plain CSVs:

- the `sar` paper's two empirical applications, copied verbatim from its
  replication package's nonproprietary export;
- the `cd` paper's Proposition 99 panel, copied from the authors' repository.

Every loader returns a `SpillPanel`: the long panel with a 0/1 `treated`
column, what its models need, and a `config_kwargs()` helper that feeds
`SCSPILLConfig` directly. For `sar` panels, what the models need is the raw
spatial weights aligned by donor label. For the `cd` panel, it is the
paper's exposed states. `config_kwargs()` configures `sar` when the panel
has spatial weights and `cd` otherwise; pass `method=` to choose. The
spatial weights are stored *unnormalized*. The estimator row-normalizes
`spatial_W` and scales `spatial_w` to sum to one, exactly as the R package
does.

## California Proposition 99

```{python}
from scspill.data import load_california

ca = load_california()
ca.df.head()
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Units | 39 U.S. states (38 donors + California) |
| Periods | 1970–2000 (annual); treatment from 1988 |
| Outcome | `cigsale` — per-capita cigarette sales (packs) |
| Covariate | `retprice` — retail cigarette price |
| `spatial_w` | California's rook-contiguity row (only Nevada = 1) |
| `spatial_W` | binary rook adjacency among the donors |

Provenance: the Abadie–Diamond–Hainmueller (2010) tobacco panel as
distributed with Cunningham's *Causal Inference: The Mixtape*; contiguity
derived from the 2024 TIGER/Line state shapefile with `spdep::poly2nb(queen
= FALSE)`.

```{python}
ca.spatial_W.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).head(5)  # most-connected donors
```

## The 2011 Sudan secession

```{python}
from scspill.data import load_sudan

sd = load_sudan()
sd.df.head(3)
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Units | 34 African countries (33 donors + "Sudan") |
| Periods | 2000–2015 (annual); treatment from 2011 |
| Outcome | `gdp_pc` — GDP per capita, constant 2015 US$ |
| Covariates | `exports_gdp_share`, `merchandise_trade_gdp_share`, `trade_gdp_share`, `clean_fuels_access`, `inflation`, `net_migration` |
| `spatial_w` | average 2000–2010 bilateral trade with Sudan (raw US$) |
| `spatial_W` | average bilateral trade among donors (raw US$) |

Provenance: World Development Indicators (percentage series stored as
proportions), with the treated unit aggregating Sudan and South Sudan after
the split; trade weights from the IMF Direction of Trade Statistics,
symmetrized and averaged over the pre-period. The loader renames the R
export's mangled WDI headers to snake_case; pass `raw_names=True` for the
original headers:

```{python}
sd.column_map
```

## Cao & Dowd's Proposition 99 panel

```{python}
from scspill.data import load_california_cd

cdp = load_california_cd(51)
cdp.df.head(3)
```

```{python}
cdp.affected_units, load_california_cd(41).affected_units
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Units | 50 U.S. states plus DC (`load_california_cd(51)`), or 41 of them (`load_california_cd(41)`) |
| Periods | 1970–2000 (annual); California treated from 1989 |
| Outcome | `cigs` — per-capita cigarette consumption (packs) |
| `affected_units` | 51 units: the twelve states that passed their own tobacco-control laws (including Arizona and Oregon) plus Nevada; 41 units: Arizona, Nevada and Oregon |
| Spatial weights | none — `config_kwargs()` configures `method="cd"` |

The 41-unit panel drops the ten policy states that do not border
California. Provenance: the input data of
[jcao0/synthetic-control-spillover](https://github.com/jcao0/synthetic-control-spillover)
at commit `86004020`, copied byte for byte (`cigs_consumption.csv` and
`state_list.csv`). It is a different sample from `load_california()`: it
keeps all 50 states and DC, and its treatment starts in 1989, not 1988. The
[case study](../prop99-spillovers.qmd) fits it.

## Using your own data

Any long panel works. Every model needs a DataFrame with unit, time,
outcome, and 0/1 treatment-indicator columns (1 for the treated unit in
post-treatment periods). Then:

- for `sar`:
  1. `spatial_w`: a Series/dict keyed by donor label (or an array in sorted
     donor order) measuring each donor's exposure to the treated unit;
  2. `spatial_W`: a labelled DataFrame (or array) of donor-to-donor weights;
  3. optionally, covariate columns.
- for `cd`: the exposed units (`affected_units`), distances
  (`unit_distances`) or a labeled exposure matrix (`effect_matrix`). Several
  treated units are allowed if they share the treatment start.

Alignment is by label wherever labels are given, so the order of your
weights never has to match the panel's — mismatched or missing donor labels
raise immediately.
